events.title: Wix IPO
events.summary: Wix began trading on NASDAQ on November 6, 2013 under ticker WIX — raising $127 million at $16.50 per share.
events.about: The IPO validated freemium website builders as a public-market category alongside Twitter's debut that same week. Wix had grown to 40 million registered users with a drag-and-drop editor that let small businesses publish without developers.

narrative.whyChosen: Wix's IPO marked website builders as a scalable public SaaS business.
narrative.whyImportant: Public capital funded international expansion and product development for no-code publishing.
narrative.problemSolved: Freemium builders needed growth capital beyond venture rounds to compete at scale.

events.title: PostCSS released
events.summary: Andrey Sitnik released PostCSS 0.1.0 on November 4, 2013 — a framework for transforming CSS with JavaScript plugins.
events.about: PostCSS parses CSS into an AST, runs plugins (Autoprefixer, cssnano, Tailwind), and outputs transformed styles — a postprocessor pipeline that works with any preprocessor or plain CSS. It became the backbone of modern front-end builds, powering millions of weekly npm downloads through webpack, Vite, and Create React App.

narrative.whyChosen: PostCSS created an extensible plugin ecosystem for CSS transformation.
narrative.whyImportant: It separated CSS authoring from build-time transforms like prefixing, minification, and future syntax.
narrative.problemSolved: Each CSS tool reinvented parsing and transformation instead of sharing a common pipeline.
